papers.title: Polytope Sampling at the Speed of Isoperimetry
papers.abstract: We give faster algorithms for sampling from the uniform distribution over a polytope. Our main result is an algorithm that, when applied to a polytope with $m$ constraints in $n$ dimensions, uses $m \cdot \mathrm{poly}\log(\frac m \delta)$ iterations, each running in time $O(mn^{\omega - 1})$, to return a sample within total variation distance $\delta$ to the uniform distribution. When $m =O(n)$ and $\delta = \mathrm{poly}(\frac 1 n)$, our runtime improves upon all prior works by an $\Omega(n^{2/3})$ factor. Our sampler is based on the recent \emph{functional stochastic localization} framework of [GST26], and achieves an iteration count nearly matching the Poincar\'e constant of the uniform distribution with respect to the logarithmic barrier.

papers.title: Rapid mixing within a phase for Ising models
papers.abstract: We study Glauber dynamics for Ising measures conditioned to have a sufficiently large majority of $+1$ spins. Under a sparse spectral width condition on the interaction matrix, we derive a Poincar\'{e} inequality for the conditioned measures from a magnetization drift condition, and a modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality from a stronger, entropy weighted condition. As applications, we obtain approximate posterior sampling in total variation distance for $\mathbb{Z}_2$ synchronization at high enough signal-to-noise ratio using $O(n\log n)$ Glauber updates from a spectral initialization. For ferromagnetic Ising models on random $d$-regular graphs, we prove rapid phase ordering down to inverse temperatures of order $1/d$, extending the temperature range of Gheissari, Sly, and Sohn (2025). Finally, we extend these inequalities to unconditioned Ising measures under an inward drift condition outside the conditioned region. This yields $O(n\log n)$ mixing of Glauber dynamics for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model at every fixed inverse temperature when the external field is sufficiently large.

papers.title: Almost Sharp Equivalence between Approximate Message Passing and Low-Degree Polynomials
papers.abstract: We prove a sharp lower bound for growing-degree polynomial estimation in the symmetric rank-one matrix estimation problem. The observation is \[ \boldsymbol{Y}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \boldsymbol{\theta} \boldsymbol{\theta}^{\top}+\boldsymbol{W}, \] where the coordinates of $\boldsymbol{\theta}$ are independent with a common, fixed sub-Gaussian distribution $\pi_\Theta$ satisfying $\mathbb E[\Theta]\neq0$, and $\boldsymbol{W}$ is symmetric with independent standard Gaussian upper-triangular entries. For every such prior, we give an explicit finite-dimensional bound implying that every sequence of polynomial estimators of degree $D(n)=o(n^{1/60})$ has normalized mean-square error with limit inferior at least $\mathbb E[\Theta^2]-q_{\mathsf{amp}}$, the limiting error of Bayes approximate message passing (AMP). This extends the constant-degree equivalence of Montanari and Wein~\cite{montanari2025equivalence} to growing degree under the same prior assumptions. Combined with their polynomial approximation of fixed-iteration AMP, the bound identifies the exact limiting low-degree MMSE whenever $D(n)\to\infty$ within this range. It thereby answers the growing-degree AMP-equivalence question discussed in~\cite{wein2025computational, maleki2026high} for nonzero-mean sub-Gaussian priors in the stated degree range. We also obtain a moment-dependent finite-dimensional lower bound for any nonzero-mean prior with all moments finite. The proof bounds low-degree MMSE using \emph{conditional} joint cumulants and a refined application of Jensen's inequality. The conditional cumulants are defined using an auxiliary Gaussian channel $\boldsymbol{R}$ calibrated to the AMP fixed point. This retains signal dependence that is lost in unconditional cumulant bounds and produces the cancellations needed for quantitative control as the degree grows.

papers.title: Singular vectors of sparse random rectangular matrices: Transition between delocalized and semilocalized phases
papers.abstract: Consider the bipartite Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi graph $\mathbb{G}(n,m,d/\sqrt{mn})$ at the critical sparsity $d = b\log(N)$ for some $b > 0$ with $N = n + m$, and constant aspect ratio $\gamma = n/m \geq 1$. We show that the spectrum of its centered and rescaled bi-adjacency matrix, whose limiting law is the Mar\v{c}enko--Pastur (MP) distribution, is split into two phases: in the bulk, singular vectors are completely delocalized, while near the edges, singular vectors are semilocalized, with their mass concentrating on small disjoint balls, centered at vertices with extreme degrees. As $b$ decreases, we identify sharp thresholds for the emergence of outlier singular values. For explicit $b_{\rm R}^{\star}$ and $b_{\rm L}^{\star}$ as functions of $\gamma$, we prove that when $b > b_{\rm R}^{\star}$, there is no outlier outside the bulk; when $b_{\rm L}^{\star}< b < b_{\rm R}^{\star}$, only right outliers emerge; and when $b < b_{\rm L}^{\star}$, outliers are present on both sides, all with high probability. This removes an extra technical condition from our previous work arxiv:2508.01456, providing a complete characterization of the parameter space. In sparser regimes, in terms of left outliers, we provide some nontrivial generating mechanisms, demonstrating that local graph structure plays a key role in understanding extreme singular values. Our proofs rely on two technical inputs: (1) an entrywise local law in the MP bulk, where the deterministic equivalent of the resolvent depends on both variance profiles and normalized vertex degrees, different from the Gaussian setting; (2) spectral radius upper bounds for nonbacktracking matrices constructed from regularized random graphs, recently developed in arXiv: 2609.26615. Our results reveal fruitful phenomena for sparse random rectangular matrices at criticality, which are beyond the universality class of their Gaussian counterparts.

papers.title: Optimal estimates for the $\ell^p$-Lipschitz constants of deep random ReLU neural networks
papers.abstract: This paper studies the $\ell^p$-Lipschitz constants of ReLU neural networks $\Phi: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ with random parameters for $p \in [1,\infty]$. The distribution of the weights follows a variant of the He initialization. In the case of zero-bias networks, we derive matching high-probability upper and lower bounds for wide networks that differ at most by an absolute constant. The bounds reveal two remarkable phenomena. First, the bounds grow root-logarithmically in terms of the depth of the net. Second, the behavior of the $\ell^p$-Lipschitz constants varies significantly between the regimes $p \in [1,2)$ and $p \in [2,\infty]$. For $p \in [2,\infty]$, the $\ell^p$-Lipschitz constant behaves similarly to $\|g\|_{p'}$, where $g \in \mathbb{R}^d$ is a standard Gaussian vector and $1/p + 1/p' = 1$. In contrast, for $p \in [1,2)$, the $\ell^p$-Lipschitz constant aligns more closely with $\|g\|_2$. For networks with possibly nonzero biases, we obtain the same lower bounds without assumptions on the bias distributions. For symmetric bias distributions with bounded densities, we also derive high-probability upper bounds for the $\ell^p$-Lipschitz constants. For fixed sub-exponential bias distributions, these upper bounds differ from the lower bounds by a factor that has square-root dependence on the depth and logarithmic dependence on the width.

papers.title: Diffusion-Based Stochastic Operator Networks for Uncertainty Quantification in Stochastic Partial Differential Equations
papers.abstract: We introduce a novel framework for uncertainty quantification of solution operators associated with stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs). Although SPDEs play a central role in modeling complex physical systems under uncertainty, their practical use typically requires specifying the magnitude and structure of model uncertainties that are often unknown and difficult to infer from noisy measurements. To address this challenge, we develop a stochastic operator-learning framework that learns directly from noisy data and outputs both a mean solution field and a quantification of uncertainty. The proposed method, namely the Stochastic Operator Network (SON), is constructed by combining the structure of the Deep Operator Network (DeepONet) with Stochastic Neural Networks (SNNs) to model stochasticity and enable probabilistic prediction. The training procedure is carried out by minimizing a Hamiltonian-type loss and optimizing the resulting objective using the Stochastic Maximum Principle. Numerical experiments on benchmark SPDEs under multiple uncertainty sources demonstrate the accuracy and robustness of the proposed method in capturing solution structure and quantifying predictive uncertainty.

papers.title: Computing Extinction Barriers in a Quorum-Sensing Reaction Network
papers.abstract: We introduce a simple reaction-network model of a quorum-sensing population that couples the cell density $x$ to the signal density $w$. In the four-channel cell-signal network studied here, scaling signal production and removal by the same factor $r$ leaves all deterministic equilibria, and their stability types, unchanged. Nevertheless, we show that $r$ shifts the quasipotential barrier $\Delta V(r)$ for rare transitions towards extinction, and thus, under metastable exit assumptions, the mean time to reach a fixed neighbourhood of the extinction state on the exponential scale $e^{N\Delta V(r)}$. We compute the barrier by minimization of the path action with the signal retained as a fluctuating coordinate, and we check it against mean extinction times obtained without the action solver, i.e., from the backward equation of the jump process on a truncated lattice and from exact stochastic simulation. Over a range of $r$, the minimum-action barriers satisfy $\Delta V(r)=\Delta V_\infty+O(1/r)$, where $\Delta V_\infty$ is obtained by eliminating the signal first, and at $r=1$ the barrier is 55% larger than $\Delta V_\infty$. A formal first-order expansion attributes this increase to the lag of the signal, of which the fluctuations of the signal remove a quarter. The saddle barrier $\Delta V(r)$ is also the least action needed to enter the basin of extinction, whereas the density threshold can be crossed more cheaply, by paths which keep the signal high and are usually followed by recovery. The mean extinction times of the backward equation, which include failed attempts, have a prefactor which tends to a constant, and they grow at a rate within $10^{-5}$ of $\Delta V(r)$ at every tested rate.

papers.title: Sharp Asymptotic Theory of Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Gaussian Processes with an RBF Kernel
papers.abstract: Gaussian processes (GPs) are widely used across machine learning, spatial statistics, time-series analysis, optimization, Bayesian statistics, and scientific applications. A central component of a GP model is its kernel, which is typically specified through a parametric family. Among the most widely used choices is the radial basis function (RBF), also known as the squared exponential or Gaussian kernel, owing to its simple form, smoothness, and flexibility. In practice, the kernel parameters are routinely estimated by the maximum likelihood estimators (MLEs), as implemented by standard GP software. Despite this widespread use, the asymptotic behavior of the MLEs remains poorly understood under fixed-domain asymptotics, even for the RBF kernel. The main difficulty arises from the increasingly strong dependence among densely sampled observations and the nonlinear dependence of the covariance matrix on the kernel parameters. In this paper, we address this gap by providing, to the best of our knowledge, the first complete asymptotic characterization of the joint MLE of the spatial variance, lengthscale, and nugget variance under fixed-domain asymptotics. We establish consistency, derive convergence rates for all three parameters, prove joint asymptotic normality, and show that these rates are minimax optimal.

papers.title: DisCo Algebra: Why Disintegration and Combination Are Not Inverses
papers.abstract: We present DisCo algebra---a compositional framework for joint probability built from a symmetric cooperad (disintegration) and a non-unital partial symmetric operad (combination restricted to the image of disintegration) on the bare family $\mathcal{P}_n=\mathrm{Prob}([0,1]^n)$. No probability integral transform, no external summary functions, no enrichment of objects with conditional kernels. The disintegration side uses block-wise joint CDFs as intrinsic, measure-determined 1D summaries, yielding a lossy compression. The combination side reads the same summaries and reconstructs via regular conditional measures, yielding a lossless embedding on admissible inputs. We prove that combination followed by disintegration is the identity on admissible inputs, but disintegration followed by combination is not---it defines a renormalization operator $R_{\mathcal{I}}=\text{Combine}\circ\text{Disintegrate}$. The information loss of this operator is exactly the probability curvature $\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{I}}(\mu)$---the conditional KL divergence between the true conditional distribution and the conditionally independent product. This curvature measures the obstruction to lossless decomposition and reveals a hard limit on how much cross-block dependence can be captured by CDF-based scalar block summaries.

papers.title: Stochastic Shockwave Dynamics in First-Order Traffic Flow
papers.abstract: Moving congestion fronts vary across realizations even when the traffic-flow law is fixed. This paper develops a generator-based formulation of the Lighthill--Whitham--Richards (LWR) model with random initial density and a deterministic fundamental diagram. Randomness enters through the initial spatial density field; every realization follows the same conservation law. For a smooth strictly concave fundamental diagram, we adapt established one-sided spatial Markov closure to traffic variables under the stated spatial-process and regularity assumptions, and derive a kinetic balance for physically normalized front intensities. Evolving the spatial generator provides density laws and congestion-front statistics without solving a road-grid problem for every realization. The formulation is continuous in physical space and time, while its numerical implementation approximates density state and integrates physical time. Four experiments distinguish deterministic consistency from stochastic comparison. Riemann and signal examples recover independently constructed exact LWR solutions. Smooth strictly concave approximations approach the deterministic triangular-diagram signal solution over the tested finite horizons; this does not establish stochastic closure at contacts or the capacity kink. A matched Monte Carlo Godunov ensemble evaluates front counts, sizes, mergers, and density distributions. The evolved generator also yields an instantaneous travel-time distribution for a frozen density field, compared with the same functional of the matched Godunov profiles. This quantity is not experienced travel time through evolving traffic. Resolution checks identify remaining normalization and small-front-loss effects. The contribution is direct evolution and interpretation of traffic-state and front distributions under a fixed first-order traffic law.

papers.title: Singular Stochastic Heat Equations with Fractional Memory
papers.abstract: We extend the paracontrolled distribution approach of Gubinelli, Imkeller, and Perkowski to singular stochastic heat equations with Caputo fractional time derivatives. By establishing Schauder estimates for the time-fractional heat flow and controlling history terms, we address the difficulties arising from temporal memory and the lack of the semigroup property. For the one-dimensional rough Burgers-type equation driven by space-time white noise with spatial dissipation \((-\Delta)^\sigma\), we prove global well-posedness for \(\sigma\in(5/6,1]\) and \(\nu\in(6\sigma/(12\sigma-5),1]\). For the heat equation with nonlinear multiplicative spatial white noise on the two-dimensional torus, we establish local well-posedness of renormalized solutions and an \(L^\infty\) blow-up criterion for every \(\nu\in(0,1]\).

papers.title: Rough Stochastic Viscous Camassa-Holm equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish well-posedness results for the viscous Camassa--Holm equation driven by the additive Gaussian noise $(1-\partial_x^2)^{-\eta}\xi$, where $\xi$ denotes the space-time white noise and $\eta>-1/12$. This formulation includes spatially colored noise for $\eta>0$, space-time white noise for $\eta=0$, and rough noise for $-1/12<\eta<0$. More precisely, we establish a pathwise solution theory via approximation by equations driven by regularized noises. The main difficulty arises from the singular interactions between the nonlinear terms and the irregular stochastic convolution. By introducing suitable enhanced stochastic objects and applying paracontrolled techniques, we obtain local well-posedness for the full range $\eta>-1/12$. Furthermore, when $\eta>1/4$, we establish global well-posedness by deriving suitable energy estimates.

papers.title: Gaussian measures under the Navier-Stokes and heat flows are mutually singular
papers.abstract: We consider the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on the torus $\mathbb{T}^d$, $d \ge 2$, with translation invariant Gaussian random initial data. We show that, for the Gaussian measure formally given by $\mu_0 \sim \exp(-\frac12 \| u \|_{\dot H^\alpha}^2)$ on divergence-free fields, its nonlinear evolution $\nu_t$ and its linear evolution $\mu_t$ are mutually singular for almost every time. Moreover, the same holds for the nonlinear evolution of an arbitrary initial measure $\nu_0$. This is in sharp contrast to the available results for Hamiltonian PDEs, where Gaussian measures are commonly quasi-invariant. We achieve this by showing that there exists a set $\mathscr G_t$ such that $\mu_t(\mathscr G_t) = 1$, but for any smooth solution of Navier-Stokes, the set of times $t$ such that $u(t) \in \mathscr G_t$ is null, which we deduce from a quantitative convexity bound for frequency-localised versions of the (typically infinite) quantity $\| \mathrm{e}^{-t \Delta} u(t) \|_{L^2}^2$.

papers.title: The semiring of spectral duality skeletons: cancellation, characters and factorization
papers.abstract: Weighted dual skeletons are the combinatorial core of spectral duality structures. Their isomorphism classes, under Cartesian product and disjoint union, form a semiring graded by the degree. We identify it completely: a class is determined by its degree, a symmetric element of the group semiring N_0[R] and its number of fixed points. Equivalently, skeletons of a given degree are finite C_2-sets over the C_2-monoid (R,+), these data are their marks, and the semiring is an infinite-monoid analogue of a crossed Burnside semiring. The multiplicative monoid is not cancellative, the only obstruction being that multiplication by a skeleton without fixed points forgets the fixed points; accordingly, the Grothendieck ring has explicit zero divisors. A continuous family of semiring characters, with the degree and the number of fixed points, is a complete invariant, and for commensurable ratios the multiplicative Grothendieck group is described by P\'olya's theorem. The main subject is factorization. The reduced monoid is atomic with bounded lengths, but factorization is not unique, the elasticity is infinite, and even the divisor-closed submonoid with one fixed point is not half-factorial. Without fixed points, every reducible skeleton splits off a single orbit, which gives a criterion by centers, exactly when the number of orbits is 8, 16, a prime or twice a prime. Irreducibility is generic in almost every type. Progression skeletons factor according to mixed-radix number systems, with all factorizations of equal length. Finally, orbit counting gives the dimension of the separatrix and the response rank of products.

papers.title: Ideal G{\aa}rding polynomials
papers.abstract: We introduce ideal G{\aa}rding polynomials, a convexity-enhanced subclass of G\aa{}rding polynomials whose G{\aa}rding components are recursively convex under partial differentiation. This class strictly contains real stable polynomials and, after translation and homogenization, lies in the Lorentzian class. Our main result is that ideal G{\aa}rding polynomials still admit a robust structure theory despite this additional convexity: they are preserved under polarization, satisfy natural closure properties, and support a linear preserver theory. A key contribution of this paper is a universal model for univariate G{\aa}rding polynomials, described by monotone root sequences and equivalently by volume polynomials of Pitman--Stanley polytopes. We establish quotient concavity, and Newton--Maclaurin type inequalities, which leads to the polarization theorem, and suggests further connections with convex geometry and Lorentzian polynomials.

papers.title: Uniform logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for the 2D Coulomb gas at the diffusive temperature scale
papers.abstract: For $N\ge2$ and $\beta>0$, consider the canonical 2D Coulomb gas ensemble \begin{equation} \mathrm{d}\mathbb{P}_{N,\beta}(Z) =\mathsf{Z}_{N,\beta}^{-1}e^{-\beta|Z|^2/2} \prod_{i<j}|z_i-z_j|^{\beta/N}\mathrm{d} Z \qquad\text{on }\mathbb{C}^N. \end{equation} The factor $N^{-1}$ in the pair exponent places the ensemble at the diffusive, or high-temperature, scale. We prove that, for every fixed inverse temperature $\beta>0$, this Gibbs measure satisfies a logarithmic Sobolev inequality (LSI) on the closed Dirichlet-form domain generated by collision-free compactly supported smooth functions, with a positive constant independent of $N$. The LSI constant may be chosen uniformly when $\beta$ ranges over a compact subset of $(0,\infty)$. A second main result establishes Poincar\'e and logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for planar Gaussian measures weighted by finite products of positive powers of distances to points, with constants depending only on the total variance of the underlying Gaussian measure and the total exponent, not on the number or locations of the points. To prove the full labeled Poincar\'e inequality, we decompose variance into permutation-invariant and label-dependent parts, controlled respectively by a weighted $\bar\partial$ estimate and by relative-coordinate conditioning with random transpositions; separately, one-site logarithmic Sobolev inequalities, a conditional entropy inequality, and a repulsive partition estimate give a defective logarithmic Sobolev inequality. Rothaus tightening combines the resulting full labeled Poincar\'e inequality with the defective logarithmic Sobolev inequality. The two main theorems on their stated closed form domains and all results used in their formal proofs, including those from the literature, have been formalized in Lean 4.

papers.title: Sharp asymptotics for the Lov\'asz number of random circulant graphs
papers.abstract: We study the LOV\'ASZ number of dense random circulant graphs generated by independent Bernoulli bits indexed by cyclic distances. Although only $O(n)$ independent random inputs determine $O(n^2)$ globally dependent edge indicators, we prove sharp expectation asymptotics along all odd orders, including composite orders, with leading constant one. This resolves a conjecture posed for random circulant graphs in 2025. The proof combines an exact Fourier reduction and complementary duality with a positive interior smoothing that reveals a nonlinear random fixed-point equation. To analyze this equation under the strong dependence of the distance-bit model, we construct canonical tree fields, establish growing-degree Gaussian approximations through polynomial comparison and Wick/Hermite expansions, and transfer the resulting approximation back to the original sign model. A deterministic residual estimate together with an explicit exceptional-event integration yields the sharp expectation asymptotics.

papers.title: Perron-Wright asymptotics and critical component processes for regular inhomogeneous random graphs
papers.abstract: We extend Wright's enumeration of connected labelled graphs with fixed surplus to irreducible critical finite type kernels and regular compact type kernels. Let $C_t(k,r)$ denote the total weight of connected labelled graphs with $k$ vertices and surplus $r$. Let $u>0$ satisfy $Ku=u$ and $\int u\,d\mu=1$, and put $\alpha=\int u^2\,d\mu$ and $\beta=\int u^3\,d\mu$. We prove that the rooted-tree radius $\rho$ is positive and real analytic near $1$, with $\rho(1)=1$ and $\log\rho(t)=\frac{\alpha^2}{2\beta}(t-1)^2+O(|t-1|^3)$, and that, for fixed $r\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ and $0\le L < \infty$, $C_t(k,r)=w_r\beta^{(r-1)/2}e^{-k}\rho(t)^{-k}k^{k+3r/2-2}\{1+O_{r,L}(k^{-1/2})\}$, uniformly for $|t-1|\le Lk^{-1/2}$, where $w_r$ is the classical Wright constant. At $t_n=1+\lambda n^{-1/3}$, these asymptotics yield local size and surplus point-process limits for deterministic finite type models and annealed compact type Bollobas-Janson-Riordan models satisfying projective quadratic regularity. After rescaling component sizes by $\beta^{1/3}n^{-2/3}$, the limit is the Aldous process at parameter $\alpha\beta^{-2/3}\lambda$, and the corresponding type profiles concentrate at the Perron law $p(dx)=u(x)\mu(dx)$. For every regular countable critical kernel, we construct graph sequences with growing finite supports and the same local limits, and identify the additive shift of the critical window caused by spectral perturbations of order $n^{-1/3}$.

papers.title: Higher-order sum rules for zeros of the planar Gaussian entire function
papers.abstract: We establish marginal sum rules for the truncated correlation functions of zeros of the planar Gaussian entire function (GEF). For each fixed integer $k\ge2$, the integral in one coordinate converges absolutely and equals $-(k-1)$ times the truncated correlation of order $k-1$. This answers the marginal-identity question posed by Krishnapur and Yogeshwaran for the planar GEF. We also prove a criterion for simple point processes under local moment and absolute integrability assumptions. Suppose there is a sequence of compactly supported cutoffs between zero and one that are eventually equal to one on each compact set. If the variances of their linear statistics tend to zero, the marginal identities hold almost everywhere. Strong clustering and variance bounds for smooth linear statistics verify these assumptions for GEF zeros. The proof uses mixed cumulants and the partition formula relating ordinary and factorial cumulants.

papers.title: The Martin boundary of the Directed Landscape
papers.abstract: In the directed landscape, the Martin boundary coincides with the horofunction boundary. We show that functions in this boundary are precisely the eternal solutions possessing a spatial growth rate, and that the minimal Martin boundary is given by the Busemann functions. Moreover, every eternal solution can be expressed as a max-plus convex combination of countably many Busemann functions. Horofunctions are exactly those eternal solutions that admit a representation in terms of at most two Busemann functions with a common growth rate. As a consequence of instability, not all horofunctions are Busemann functions, and the Martin boundary is strictly larger than its minimal part.

papers.title: Differentiability of the Leading Lyapunov Exponent of a linear differential equation with random coefficients Application to the Calculation of the Selection Gradient in Random Environments
papers.abstract: The study of evolution in temporally fluctuating environments often relies on the analysis of Lyapunov exponents, which quantify the exponential growth of populations. However, when model parameters depend on a stochastic process, calculating the selection gradient, a key tool for predicting the evolution of phenotypic traits, becomes a mathematical challenge. While the periodic case has been resolved, a general approach for random environments remains to be developed. This article proposes a rigorous method to: Establish the differentiability of the leading Lyapunov exponent with respect to a parameter, providing an explicit integral formula for its derivative. Develop a numerical algorithm to approximate the derivative by solving an extended differential equation. Apply these results to the analysis of mutant invasion in a resident population at equilibrium, identifying the selection gradient as the derivative of the top Lyapunov exponent.

papers.title: Space-filling curves and small-ball probabilities for the Kloosterman process
papers.abstract: We construct explicitly a space-filling curve in the support of the limiting Kloosterman process, using the planar partial-sum curve of the Rudin--Shapiro sequence. The qualitative existence statement was previously attributed to J. Bober by Kowalski. The resulting curve is a closed, $1/2$-H\"older continuous loop whose image contains a specified triangle of area $1/128$. Its Fourier coefficients are purely imaginary and satisfy $|\widehat f(h)|\leq(2\pi|h|)^{-1}$ for $h\ne 0$. We also prove a uniform lower bound for small balls centred at closed $1/2$-H\"older curves with a fixed coefficient bound, of the form $\exp\{-C\varepsilon^{-2}\log^2(2/\varepsilon)\}$. Known functional convergence then gives a quantitative lower bound for the limiting proportion of two-parameter Kloosterman paths approximating the constructed loop.

papers.title: Poisson-Dirichlet statistics for the log-modulus of the Riemann zeta function on expanding intervals near the critical line
papers.abstract: For $T > 0$ large, let $\tau$ be uniformly distributed on $[T,2T]$ and let $\sigma = \sigma(T)$ be a deterministic real part approaching $1/2$ from the right. For the Riemann zeta function $\zeta$, we study the Gibbs measure with density proportional to $|\zeta(\sigma + \mathrm{i}\tau + \mathrm{i} h)|^{\beta}$ on $I_{\theta} := [ - (\log{T})^{\theta},(\log{T})^{\theta}]$, for every $\theta > 0$ and $\beta > 0$. As $\beta$ increases, the Gibbs measure increasingly favors positions where $|\zeta|$ is large, providing a way to study the spatial organization of extreme values. Under explicit conditions on the rate at which $\sigma$ approaches the critical line, a phase transition is established at the critical inverse temperature $\beta_{c}(\theta) := 2\sqrt{1 + \theta}$. The limiting distribution of the correlation (or overlap) between the field values at two positions sampled from the Gibbs measure is concentrated at $0$ when $\beta \leq \beta_{c}(\theta)$, and assigns masses $\beta_{c}(\theta)/\beta$ and $1 - \beta_{c}(\theta)/\beta$ to $0$ and $1$, respectively, when $\beta > \beta_{c}(\theta)$. Joint convergence of the overlaps is also established, with the limiting arrays described by Poisson-Dirichlet weights in the low-temperature regime. The Ghirlanda-Guerra identities, which provide recursive relations for the joint overlap distributions, are established in the limit, uniformly for bounded deterministic observables of the sampled positions. All our results are established independently of the Riemann hypothesis.

papers.title: Recursive Operator Localization and Spectral Gap Descent via the Geometry of Local Spectral Expansion
papers.abstract: We introduce Recursive Operator Localization (ROL), a framework for constructing hierarchies of local energy problems linked by linear maps between Hilbert spaces. To address spectral-gap problems, including those arising in quantum systems, we study a realization of ROL by nested subspaces indexed by a weighted simplicial complex. Using spectral gaps of auxiliary classical random walks on links, we propagate geometric estimates upward and use them to turn local spectral gaps at the bottom of the hierarchy into a spectral-gap bound for the global operator. For weighted scalar-valued functions on facets, the ROL decomposition becomes the law of total variance, recovering classical spectral-gap bounds from local link expansion (Alev and Lau, STOC 2020). Moreover, for positive binary spin distributions, conditional influence describes the overlap of the corresponding subspaces, yielding known heat-bath gap bounds from spectral independence (Anari, Liu, and Oveis Gharan, FOCS 2020). The framework also offers a route toward quantum Gibbs sampling, with applications requiring model-specific geometric estimates and energy comparisons.

papers.title: A Universal Lower Bound for the Complexity of Gaussian-Divisible Spin Glasses
papers.abstract: We consider a variant of the spherical mixed spin glass model with non-Gaussian disorder. Specifically, we replace the usual standard Gaussian interaction coefficients with Gaussian-divisible ones, meaning that each coefficient can be expressed as the sum of a standard Gaussian random variable and an independent, non-Gaussian random variable. We show that the annealed complexity of this model is at least the annealed complexity of the standard Gaussian model, if the non-Gaussian part is centered and subexponential.

papers.title: Analyticity of the correlation length in subcritical FK-percolation and Potts models
papers.abstract: We prove that the correlation length of FK-percolation and Potts models on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ is analytic in the whole subcritical regime of parameters. Our proof makes use of the identification of the polar dual of the mass with the solution of an equation involving the leading eigenvalue of the FK--Ruelle operator, introduced in the context of Ornstein--Zernike theory in Campanino, Ioffe and Velenik (Probab. Theory Relat. Fields, 2003), and crucially relies on Kato's theory of analytic perturbation of linear operators. As a consequence of this result, we prove that the correlation length cannot be invariant by rotation except at countably many values of the temperature parameter in the subcritical phase.

papers.title: Singularity and regularity of the critical 2D Stochastic Heat Flow
papers.abstract: The Critical 2D Stochastic Heat Flow (SHF) provides a natural candidate solution to the ill-posed 2D Stochastic Heat Equation with multiplicative space-time white noise. In this paper, we initiate the investigation of the spatial properties of the SHF. We prove that, as a random measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$, it is a.s. singular w.r.t. the Lebesgue measure. This is obtained by probing a "quasi-critical" regime and showing the asymptotic log-normality of the mass assigned to vanishing balls, as the disorder strength is sent to zero at a suitable rate, accompanied by similar results for critical 2D directed polymers. We also describe the regularity of the SHF, showing that it is a.s. H\"older $C^{-\epsilon}$ for any $\epsilon>0$, implying the absence of atoms, and we establish local convergence to zero in the long time limit.

papers.title: On the pair correlation function of the Sine$_\beta$ process
papers.abstract: We study the Sine$_\beta$ process, the bulk point process scaling limit of beta-ensembles. We provide a representation of its pair correlation function for all $\beta>0$ via a stochastic differential equation, and also via an infinite system of differential equations. We show that the pair correlation function is continuous in $\beta$, and provide estimates for its asymptotic decay. When $\beta=2n$ is an even integer, we characterize the pair correlation function through a linear system of $n$ ordinary differential equations and derive the function's power series expansion. Our results recover the classical explicit formula for the pair correlation function in the $\beta=2$ and $4$ cases. We obtain our results by studying the one-point function of the $\operatorname{HP}_{\beta,\delta}$ process, the point process limit of the circular Jacobi beta-ensemble.

papers.title: Quadratic mixing for the Lee--Sidford Dikin walk
papers.abstract: Let $K=\{x\in\R^d:Ax\ge b\}$ be a bounded full-dimensional polytope with $m$ inequalities. For targets on $K$ with density proportional to $\exp(-\vartheta^\transpose x)$, we prove a $\widetilde O(d^2)$ bound, measured in Markov chain iterations, for the chi-square mixing of the $1/2$-lazy Metropolis Dikin walk based on a polylogarithmically rescaled Lee--Sidford metric. The estimate holds for every initial law with finite chi-square divergence. The proof controls the reverse Gaussian proposal through a quantitative average self-concordance estimate at the required $O(1/d)$ scale. We establish this estimate from uniform analytic derivative bounds for the Lewis-weight subspace and an all-order projection-weighted contraction inequality for Gaussian chaoses. For order $j$, the latter bounds each base-point polynomial at scale $d^{j/2}$, up to $j$-dependent and logarithmic factors. Truncating at logarithmic order then absorbs the remaining pathwise loss. This resolves, in the affirmative, the open problem of whether the Gaussian Lee--Sidford Dikin walk mixes in $\widetilde O(d^2)$ iterations: the previously stated quadratic bounds \cite[Theorem~1.4]{LLV20}, \cite[Theorem~1.2]{GKM24} rest on reverse-proposal steps identified as unresolved in \cite[Section~1]{Kook26}, whose $\widetilde O(d^{9/4})$ bound was the best rigorously established rate prior to this work. The proof is found by ChatGPT 5.6 Pro.

papers.title: Strict monotonicity of weighted inhomogeneous percolation thresholds under covering maps
papers.abstract: We study Bernoulli bond percolation under weak covering maps for a class of weighted inhomogeneous product measures such that each edge $e$ carries a positive weight $w(e)$ and is open at intensity $\lambda\geq 0$ with probability $1-\exp(-\lambda w(e))$. We prove a strict monotonicity of the weighted critical intensities $\lambda_c$ in the covering compatibility setting under bounded degree, uniform ellipticity, tame fibre and disjoint tree-lifting. While for the weighted uniform connection thresholds $\lambda_{\mathrm{conn}}$, we establish their strict monotonicity for non-injective weak covering maps under bounded degree, covering compatibility, uniform ellipticity, bounded-fibre and disjoint tree-lifting. Moreover, we verify a general-profile theorem on strict monotonicities of the two thresholds $\lambda_c$ and $\lambda_{\mathrm{conn}}$ respectively under explicit compact-interval finite-energy, derivative bounds and aforementioned geometric conditions.
